To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cost of completion is a major determinant of the decision to complete, that the cost of the investment already made is a minor determinant, and that the cost remaining to complete is a minor determinant.

(1) the cost of completion is not the only relevant consideration in decisions to complete, (2) the cost of completing a partially completed project is not the sum of all costs to that point plus costs of completion, (3) the cost of continuing is the cost of the next payment, plus the value of the project if completed, and (4) the cost of stopping is the value of the investment made to that point.

(a) the cost-to-complete is a more powerful determinant of completion than the expected value; (b) the cost-to- complete is more powerful than expected value even when it is known to be less accurate as a predictor; and (c) the cost-to complete is more powerful when it is known that it is less accurate as a prediction than when it is known only that it may be less accurate.
